Contaminated or unsuitable soil

Land remediation, ground that cannot stay, classified before it moves

Removing and disposing of contaminated or unsuitable soil and restoring the site. The material is classified first, because the classification decides where it can legally go, and where it goes is almost always the largest line on the job. Send the classification report, and we will price removal, cartage and validation.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Site assessment and classification

    Who You, through an environmental consultant

    What is in the ground and how far it goes. Deliberately not us: the person defining how much comes out should not be the person paid to take it out.

  2. 02

    Extent defined

    Who Your consultant

    Laterally and in depth. Without a defined extent the excavation has no edge.

  3. 03

    Validation plan agreed

    Who You, through your consultant

    How the site is shown to be clean afterwards. Agreed before digging, not after.

  4. 04

    Disposal facilities confirmed

    Who Max

    A facility licensed for that classification, confirmed before the first load.

  5. 05

    Controls for the open excavation

    Who Max

    Dust suppression, covering, exclusion zones and runoff control.

  6. 06

    Backfill material decided

    Who You, with your engineer

    What goes back in, and to what compaction, once the hole is validated.

The detail

Why remediation prices come with rates rather than figures

  • The extent is an estimate until it is dug. A defined extent from a consultant is a good estimate, and ground does not always respect it.
  • The classification sets the destination. And the destination sets the cartage distance, which is a real part of the cost.
  • Soil is heavy. A small area to depth generates large tonnage very quickly.
  • Mixing classifications is expensive. One load of the worst material contaminates the rate for everything it travels with.
  • The hole cannot close early. Backfilling before validation sampling means digging it out again.
  • Water collects. An open excavation fills, and that water usually needs classifying too.

What we need to quote it

The address
So we can look at access and what is around it
Photographs
One from the street and one of the work itself
Any reports you hold
Hazardous materials, structural, survey or levels
Your dates
What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

If the contamination is asbestos, the pathway changes

Asbestos contaminated soil is handled by licensed asbestos removalists under the asbestos pathway, not as general remediation.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

What makes soil unsuitable rather than contaminated?
Unsuitable soil is material that cannot perform structurally, such as uncontrolled fill or organic material. Contaminated soil contains something that makes it a risk. They are different problems with different pathways, and a consultant tells them apart.
Who classifies it?
An environmental consultant engaged by you. We do not classify material we are being paid to remove, and you should not want us to.
Can you quote a fixed price?
For a defined extent and a confirmed classification, close to it. Where the extent is uncertain the excavation and disposal are priced on agreed rates so the exposure is visible rather than buried in a contingency.
What goes back in the hole?
Clean fill, VENM or an engineered fill to your engineer’s specification, placed in layers and compacted. Not whatever is nearest.
How do I prove the site is clean afterwards?
Your consultant’s validation report, supported by our disposal dockets. A future purchaser or lender may ask for both.

Get a quote

Send the consultant report if you have one

The classification and the extent are what make remediation quotable. If you do not have them, tell us what was found and we will tell you what the next step is.

  • Excavation and disposal priced on rates agreed before we start
  • Classifications kept apart rather than carted as one
  • Backfill and compaction quoted once the validated extent is known
